extraction.name: OpenThoughts3
extraction.description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a state-of-the-art open-data SFT reasoning dataset composed of science, math, and code data, created to train reasoning models via supervised fine-tuning.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, Ashima Suvama, Benjamin Feuer, Liangyu Chen, Zaid Khan, Eric Frankel, Sachin Grover, Caroline Choi, Niklas Muennighoff, Shiye Su, Wanjia Zhao, John Yang, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Kartik Sharma, Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji, Yichuan Deng, Sarah Pratt, Vivek Ramanujan, Jon Saad-Falcon, Jeffrey Li, Achal Dave, Alon Albalak, Kushal Arora, Blake Wulfe, Chinmay Hegde, Greg Durrett, Sewoong Oh, Mohit Bansal, Saadia Gabriel, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Vaishaal Shankar, Aaron Gokaslan, Mike A. Merrill, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Yejin Choi, Jenia Jitsev, Reinhard Heckel, Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created using a systematic data generation pipeline involving sourcing questions from existing and newly generated datasets, mixing questions from top-performing sources, filtering for high-quality questions using LLMs or fastText, deduplicating questions, sampling multiple answers per question from a teacher model, and filtering out low-quality answers. The process involved over 1,000 controlled experiments to optimize each step.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from 27 different sources for code, 21 for math, and 14 for science. Sources included StackExchange (CodeGolf, Physics), OpenCodeReasoning, OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath, Organic Chemistry PDFs, and others. Answers were generated by teacher models (QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The pipeline included sourcing questions, mixing top sources, filtering questions (difficulty-based or response length), deduplicating questions (exact or fuzzy), sampling multiple answers (1x, 4x, 16x), and filtering answers (though final pipeline skipped answer filtering as it did not improve performance).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered using LLM-based difficulty assessment or response length. Questions were deduplicated using exact match or fuzzy string similarity. Answers were generated by querying teacher models multiple times. Decontamination was performed against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity and N-gram similarity to remove contaminated samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers and reasoning traces were generated by teacher models (QwQ-32B and DeepSeek-R1). For OpenThoughts3, QwQ-32B was used as the primary teacher. Multiple answers were sampled per question (16x). No manual human annotation was performed for the final dataset; it relied on automated generation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper notes that models with better performance are not necessarily better teachers (QwQ-32B outperformed DeepSeek-R1 despite lower benchmark scores). It also found that answer filtering did not significantly improve performance compared to using all samples.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and models are available on openthoughts.ai and Hugging Face. The project is part of the OpenThoughts project which releases iterative generations of datasets and models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to demystify SFT data curation for reasoning models and provide open-source alternatives to proprietary datasets. It highlights a trade-off between reasoning capabilities and safety, noting that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data can degrade preexisting safety alignment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is composed of math, code, and science questions. The paper notes that limited question diversity has relatively little impact on performance if answer diversity is high. It also observes that training on math data improves science performance, suggesting cross-domain transfer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not include reinforcement learning data. It does not explore staged SFT or curriculum learning. The models trained on this data show degraded safety alignment compared to base models. The dataset is limited to math, code, and science domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Fine Tuning. Specifically for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of reasoning models in math, code, and science domains.
